{{Quote|Whatever it is, it's dumping G-waves like a singularity—but the screens don't pick up any other anomalies ...|A Rebel Operative|<ref name="ASG" />}}
The '''collector-repulsor array''', also referred to simply as the '''repulsor ray''', was a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] under development by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. It would focus the [[G-wave]]s of hundreds of [[repulsor projector]]s to distort [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] crusts, with cataclysmic results.

==Description==
The collector-repulsor array consisted of a large concave surface resembling an extremely large [[Rectenna/Legends|scanning bowl]] for a [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|sub-space communications]] [[Subspace relay station/Legends|relay]], and hundreds of low-yield [[repulsor projector]]s. The bowl acted as a collector for the G-wave emissions of the projectors, generating a field that could distort [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] crustal pressures, producing devastating [[Groundquake/Legends|earthquakes]] and [[Volcano/Legends|volcanic eruptions]]. While lacking the [[Mundicide|planet-obliterating]] capabilities of a [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], it was much less expensive, and still capable of destroying entire civilizations. Further, the entire collector-repulsor array could be transported in a small [[Starship/Legends|ship]], and deployed into [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of the target world within [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]].<ref name="ASG" />

==History==
[[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance HQ]] became aware of a fully operational [[Unidentified Imperial asteroid base|Imperial base]] located on an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] far from the nearest areas of conflict between the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] and the Empire, and dispatched a ship with a group of Rebels to investigate. On approach, the Rebels detected an efflux of G-waves comparable to a [[Singularity (physics)|singularity]], but no other anomalies; they found this to be odd, but convenient, as the [[Gravity/Legends|gravitational]] noise would mask the signatures of the [[Verpine/Legends|Verpine]]-built [[Grav-bike/Legends|grav-bikes]] they were carrying, hypothetically allowing for a swift and uneventful insertion and exfiltration.<ref name="ASG" />
{{RPGseed}}
The Rebels parked their ship in orbit, descended to the asteroid base, and investigated. They found a facility manufacturing a large volume of low-yield [[Repulsorlift motor|repulsor motors]], another facility building what seemed to be an unusually large sub-space communications relay scanning bowl, residential and recreational accommodations for the [[Factory/Legends|factory]] workers, and a high-security underground [[Laboratory/Legends|laboratory]] deep within the asteroid.<ref name="ASG" />

After infiltrating the laboratory, the Rebels discovered the purpose of the products being manufactured in the rest of the base was to create a new, civilization-ending collector-repulsor array. They availed themselves of the chance to destroy the delicate control systems of the weapon, and then, in the confusion, escaped the laboratory in a running [[Lightfight|gunfight]]. From there, they were presented with the opportunity to either return to their ship on their grav-bikes, or damage the base further by appropriating and using an Imperial [[Warship/Legends|warship]].<ref name="ASG" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
The collector-repulsor array is the focus of "[[Ain't Science Grand?]]," the seventh adventure seed presented in the [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|first edition]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]].
